newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey disputes U.S. human rights criticism.
newsitem.headline: Turkey disputes U.S. human rights criticism.

text.p: Turkey on Friday denied U.S. accusations that its human rights record was faltering and said parts of a State Department rights report on Turkey were "unacceptable".

"Turkey has made noteworthy advances in the human rights issue in 1996," the foreign ministry said in a statement. It listed human rights education for the security forces and legal action against suspected rights abusers as improvements.

Washington criticised NATO ally Ankara in its annual report on human rights worldwide released on Thursday. It said Turkey still had grave human rights problems last year and that the situation had gone downhill in some ways.
"The report says that serious problems are continuing. But the data and opinions put forward do not support this," the Turkish statement said.

The U.S. report cited the situation in southeastern Turkey, where most of the Kurdish population lives, as an area of "particular concern (because Ankara) has long denied its Kurdish population ... basic cultural and linguistic rights."
It accused Ankara of forcibly displacing an estimated 560,000 noncombatants in its campaign against Kurdistan Workers' Party rebels.
The Turkish foreign ministry said the report was based partly on information from Turkish and foreign human rights groups that are biased towards Ankara.
It said Turkey rejected accusations, levelled by some foreign non-governmental organisations (NGOs), of rights violations against them.

"Allegations by certain NGOs abroad that Turkey harasses human rights monitors, lawyers and doctors are unacceptable," the ministry said. Turkey says foreign groups like Amnesty International and Human Rights Watch are biased against it.
